high.title: Topic cards lack per-card 'Open in reader' quick actions (wave11 gap)
high.observation: On /topics index and /topics/[topicId], each topic/source card is a single Link to the topic or source detail page. There is no secondary 'Open in reader' affordance on individual cards. A single 'Read topic' button exists at the topic detail header level only.
high.impact: Users exploring topics must navigate to a detail page before reaching the reader. Discovery friction; inconsistent with search-results which surfaces 'Open in reader' for sources.
high.recommendation: Add a compact 'Open in reader' secondary link or icon button on each topic card (index) and on source cards within a topic page, linking to /reader?topics=<id> or /reader?feed=<id>. Keep primary card click for detail if needed, or make the whole card go to reader with a detail affordance.

high.title: Topic detail source cards have no reader handoff; only source page navigation
high.observation: On /topics/agents, the 21 source cards link exclusively to /sources/* pages. The only reader entry is the header-level 'Read topic' button. No per-source quick entry to filtered reader.
high.impact: Users who arrived via topic discovery cannot directly open a specific source in the reader from the topic page; must go through source detail or global reader.
high.recommendation: Add an 'Open in reader' link on each source card within topic pages (or an icon button) that constructs /reader?feed=<sourceId>. Consider exposing recent article count as a hint.

medium.title: ArticleTeaser 'Open' link targets article page, not reader (handoff inconsistency)
medium.observation: Search results render ArticleTeaser components. The trailing 'Open' link navigates to getArticlePath (article detail page). There is a top-level 'Continue in reader' when a query exists, but no per-result reader entry.
medium.impact: Search discovery does not feed the reader directly per item. Users expecting 'search then read' must either use the coarse 'Continue in reader' or leave the search context.
medium.recommendation: Add a per-result 'Read in reader' action on ArticleTeaser (or search result items) that links to /reader with appropriate filters (q, source, etc.). Keep 'Open' for article page if desired as secondary.

medium.title: Search 'Continue in reader' CTA uses identical surface styling to Search button
medium.observation: Both the form submit button and the 'Continue in reader' link (when query present) use: rounded-xl border border-(--line) bg-(--surface) px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium. They sit in adjacent surface-card containers and can appear as peer actions rather than progressive disclosure.
medium.impact: Weak visual distinction between 'search again' and 'switch to reader'. Users may not perceive the intended handoff escalation.
medium.recommendation: Differentiate the handoff CTA: use primary/brand treatment, or an arrow icon, or place it as a prominent inline banner. Consider labeling it 'Open results in reader' for clarity.

low.title: Topics index renders as flat list rows on mobile; no card separation or tap-target affordance
low.observation: At 390x844 the /topics page shows a long vertical list of topic rows with subtle dividers. Rows are full-width, flat, without card chrome. While touch targets are adequate, the presentation does not communicate 'selectable collection' as strongly as desktop grid cards.
low.impact: Slightly reduced perceived interactivity and grouping on mobile discovery. May feel like plain text navigation rather than content collections.
low.recommendation: Consider subtle card or surface treatment for topic rows on narrow viewports, or at minimum ensure chevron + count are strongly right-aligned and provide clear press feedback.

low.title: All topic cards have uniform visual weight regardless of source count
low.observation: On /topics desktop grid, cards for 'Research (73)' and 'Blogs (63)' look identical in size/emphasis to 'Reasoning Models (0)' or 'Fairness (0)'. The only signal is a small secondary badge.
low.impact: Users scanning for high-value collections must read numbers rather than perceive density via layout. Popular topics not visually prioritized.
low.recommendation: Optional: scale subtle visual weight (padding, border, or badge prominence) for high-count topics, or surface a 'Popular' section. Keep accessibility and tap parity.

nit.title: Search input and 'Search' button have tight padding on mobile; may benefit from larger tap targets
nit.observation: The search form uses py-2 on input and standard button padding. On 390px in dark, the row is compact; the submit button text 'Search' is short but the overall control height is modest.
nit.impact: Minor; current targets meet basic usability but are not generous.
nit.recommendation: Increase min-height to ~44px or add py-2.5/3 on the form row for mobile.
